title: SlimSnap Export
description: Structured screenshot output for AI agents — pasteable as text into terminal-based agents like Claude Code, Aider, and Codex CLI. v2 introduces frames: a regular screenshot is one frame; a scrollable capture is several frames stacked vertically, each with its own coordinate space.

schema_version.description: SlimSnap schema version. Increment on breaking changes.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when the screenshot was captured.

mode.description: 'single' for a regular screenshot (one frame), 'scroll' for a scrollable capture (one frame per page).

capture.description: Total pixel dimensions of the whole capture (all frames stacked).

screen.description: Optional metadata about the captured surface.

url.description: URL if the captured surface was a web page.

frames.description: The content, top to bottom. A single screenshot has exactly one frame. All coordinates inside a frame are normalized 0-1 against that frame's dims.

ai_enrichment.description: Optional LLM-generated metadata (intent, suggested actions). Absent or null if not enriched.

estimated_tokens.description: Approximate token count when this JSON is fed to an LLM.

kind.description: 'spatial' frames stack vertically. Reserved for future temporal (video) frames.

dims.description: Pixel dimensions of THIS frame. Coordinates inside the frame are normalized against these.

scroll_y_px.description: Pixel offset of this frame's top edge from the top of the whole capture.

images.description: Image files backing this frame. Present only when images were saved to disk; inline/copied JSON omits it.

offset_y_px.description: Offset of this image inside the frame.

elements.description: Detected UI elements with OCR text and bounding boxes, in this frame's coordinate space.

annotations.description: User-drawn annotations in this frame's coordinate space.

bbox.description: [x, y, width, height] in normalized 0-1 coordinates relative to the FRAME.

point.description: [x, y] in normalized 0-1 coordinates relative to the FRAME.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across ALL frames of the capture.

value.description: Text content or structured value of the element.

color.description: Average color of the element region, e.g. '#3B82F6'.

target_ref.description: ID of the element this annotation references. IDs are unique across frames, so this may point into an adjacent frame when the target sits on a frame boundary.
